title: Java Create Files
learningObjectives: Create a new empty file with File.createNewFile.
Understand the boolean result when a file already exists.
Create directories using mkdir and mkdirs.
Check creation results before using a new path.

understand.concept: Java can create a new empty file with File.createNewFile. The method returns true when it creates the file and false when the path already exists; it can throw IOException when creation fails. For directories, mkdir creates one level while mkdirs can create missing parent levels. A program should check return values and handle exceptions rather than assuming the operation succeeded.
understand.whyItMatters: File handling allows a Java application to persist, retrieve and manage information beyond the lifetime of a single run.
understand.analogy: Think of a path as a labeled address to a storage location; the address and the data stored there are different things.
understand.analogyLimit: A path is not a guarantee that the target exists or that the program has permission to access it.

explain.narrative: Create a File for the desired path, then call createNewFile inside a try/catch because it declares IOException. A true result means this call created the file; false means the path already existed. Use mkdir for one directory and mkdirs for a nested path. Choose a safe, application-controlled location and avoid treating user-supplied paths as trusted.

examples.title: Create an empty file
examples.explanation: createNewFile creates an empty file when the path is new and reports the result.

examples.title: Create an existing file twice
examples.explanation: The second call returns false because the file created by the first call already exists.

examples.title: Create one directory
examples.code:
import java.io.File;
public class Main { public static void main(String[] args) { File folder = new File("single-folder"); System.out.println(folder.mkdir()); } }
examples.explanation: mkdir creates the final directory when its parent already exists.

examples.title: Create nested directories
examples.code:
import java.io.File;
public class Main { public static void main(String[] args) { File folder = new File("parent/child/grandchild"); System.out.println(folder.mkdirs()); System.out.println(folder.isDirectory()); } }
examples.explanation: mkdirs creates missing parent directories as well as the requested final directory.

examples.title: Create file and inspect length
examples.explanation: A newly created empty file has a length of zero bytes.

hints: Start with a Path or File that points to a controlled test location.
Use try-with-resources for streams and writers, and handle IOException where the API declares it.
Test both the normal case and an edge case such as a missing path or existing target.
